name: CogArena
description: CogArena v1: a benchmark of ten interactive jsPsych behavioral experiments for evaluating multimodal AI agents through a real browser, with three-level scoring (completion, accuracy vs. literature-derived human baselines, and behavioral signatures via statistical tests).
citeAs: Fernandez, K., Chen, C., Zhou, J., Sadowski, B., Miceli, A. C., & Krajbich, I. (2026). CogArena: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents on Interactive Behavioral Experiments. NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track (under review).
rai:dataCollection: Tasks are ported from vetted research codebases (cited per task in the paper). Trial-data records in this dataset come from the empirical study reported in the accompanying paper: each record is one (model, task, session) triple, where the agent is a closed- or open-weight large language model invoked through a single shared scaffold (Browser-Use). No human-subject data is included in this release.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses: (i) evaluating new multimodal agents on the v1 task set; (ii) reproducing the headline study reported in the paper; (iii) extending the Level 3 scoring layer to additional behavioral signatures within the v1 tasks. Out-of-scope: (i) using the human baselines as ground truth for training models to mimic human behavior outside the explicit signature contracts; (ii) training models specifically to evade Level 3 detection.
rai:dataLimitations: Human baselines are drawn from published literature, not from humans recruited on the CogArena platform. The v1 task set is ten curated tasks; agents that succeed on all ten do not necessarily generalize to the broader cognitive-science literature.
rai:dataBiases: The Level 2 accuracy and Level 3 behavioral signatures are calibrated against human baselines drawn from published cognitive-psychology and behavioral-economics studies, the participant pools of which are predominantly WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) and recruited via online platforms (Prolific, MTurk) or Western university subject pools. Effect sizes elicited in those samples may not generalize to other populations, and "human-aligned" agent behavior on CogArena should be interpreted as alignment with these particular baselines rather than with humans in general. Task selection within the v1 set itself reflects what is well-characterized in the cited literatures, which skews toward English-language verbal stimuli, Western moral framings (e.g. moral_machine), and Western financial intuitions (e.g. dictator/risky-choice games).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. CogArena does not collect human-subject data; every record in the scored-sessions dataset is the output of a software agent (LLM) acting on a deterministic experimental paradigm. Session identifiers are random UUIDs that do not link to any real person. The literature-derived human baselines used for L2 scoring are summary statistics (means, standard deviations, effect sizes) extracted from published papers, not raw participant data.
rai:dataSocialImpact: CogArena is intended as a measurement and auditing tool for evaluating whether AI agents reproduce canonical human cognitive signatures, motivated by recent demonstrations that AI agents can produce data that is indistinguishable from human responses on online behavioral tasks. Positive impact: provides researchers running online experiments with a standardized way to measure agent susceptibility on their tasks, supporting the integrity of the broader behavioral-data ecosystem. Risks: (i) the same scoring contracts could be inverted to fine-tune models specifically to reproduce the published signatures (this misuse is explicitly out-of-scope per rai:dataUseCases); (ii) publicly listing tasks and signatures may make naive contamination attacks easier in the short term, though we believe the long-run benefit of standardized, verifiable evaluation outweighs this. The benchmark does not target or evaluate any human individual or demographic group.
rai:hasSyntheticData: Yes. All trial-data records in the scored-sessions distribution are synthetic in the sense that they are produced by AI agents (closed- or open-weight LLMs running through the Browser-Use scaffold) interacting with the experimental paradigms; no human participant trials are included. Human baselines used for Level 2 scoring are summary statistics derived from published human studies, not synthetic.

distribution.name: code-archive
distribution.description: Source code archive pinned to the v1.0.0 release tag (immutable; sha256 will not drift as main advances). Tasks, scoring pipeline, agents, and committed reference results.

distribution.name: task-configs
distribution.description: Per-task configuration JSONs describing each experimental paradigm.

distribution.name: scoring-specs
distribution.description: Per-task Level 2 metric and Level 3 signature specifications.

distribution.name: results-csv
distribution.description: Reference scored-session CSVs (random-agent chance floor and frontier-model pilot).

recordSet.name: tasks
recordSet.description: Metadata record for each task in the catalog (task_id, cognitive domain, upstream source repository).

field.name: task_id
field.description: Unique task identifier matching the directory name under tasks/.

field.name: domain
field.description: Cognitive domain category (e.g. perception, learning, risk_ambiguity, social_economic, memory_recall, memory_recognition, foraging, compositional, moral, judgment).

field.name: source_repo
field.description: URL of the upstream research repository the task was ported from.

field.name: citation
field.description: Primary literature reference for the paradigm.

recordSet.name: scored-sessions
recordSet.description: One record per scored (model, task, repeat) triple from the empirical study. Sources from results/*.csv (the random-floor and frontier-pilot CSVs committed in the repo).

field.name: run_index
field.description: Sequential index assigned by the harness sweep runner.

field.name: repeat_index
field.description: Repeat number for the (model, task) cell, zero-indexed.

field.name: model_id
field.description: Identifier of the agent model (e.g. random, gemini-3-flash-preview, grok-4.1-fast, glm-4.6v).

field.name: rc
field.description: Process exit code: 0 = successful run, non-zero = timeout or schema-rejection failure.

field.name: wall_time
field.description: Wall-clock seconds for the agent run.

field.name: composite
field.description: Composite CogArena score in [0, 100], computed as 100 * (0.15*L1 + 0.35*L2 + 0.50*L3).

field.name: l1
field.description: Level 1 (completion) score in [0, 1]: fraction of required trials answered with a valid key/click.

field.name: l2
field.description: Level 2 (accuracy) score in [0, 1]: agent performance metric vs. literature-derived human baseline.

field.name: l3
field.description: Level 3 (behavioral signature) score in [0, 1]: weighted alignment with canonical task-specific effects.
